::: {.callout-note title="Before you start"}
Complete [Connect coordinate domains](titin-coordinate-domains.qmd) first.
Read [Combine point clouds and analytical geometries](mixed-model-evaluation.qmd)
for connecting coordinate clouds to analytical subunits. You should understand training versus held-point residuals and why
a lower training error alone does not establish a better model. This is an
advanced application; the expensive calculations are available through the
generator rather than repeated during rendering.
:::

We now ask whether atomic form factors, displaced solvent, and hydration
explain the remaining residuals. Start with the fixed-control table; only then
consider allowing solvent parameters to vary.

## Load the saved calculation

Run the setup below in a fresh kernel from `docs/tutorials` in a repository
checkout. It verifies the shared inputs, outputs, and calculation source, then
loads numerical curves and viewer helpers. It does not execute previous fits.
For dependencies and full regeneration, see
[Reproduce the saved calculations](fit-linked-titin.qmd#reproduce-the-saved-calculations).
The disabled fitting cells build on earlier stages when executed by
`python Examples/generate_linked_titin.py` from the repository root.

## Separate atomic and solvent contributions

We now keep the heavy-atom resolution and change the scattering weights.
The local extract also provides models 7, 13 and 19 of the 1TIU NMR ensemble;
we average these with model 1 to include a small amount of domain flexibility.
This changes both the domain sampling and the scattering physics relative to
step 2. Within the atomic controls below, all six models use the same four
conformations, so their differences isolate the solvent terms.

`AtomicSAXSCloud` assigns q-dependent Cromer--Mann form factors, standard
implicit protein hydrogens, and a Gaussian excluded-solvent contribution to
each heavy-atom group. The default solvent electron density is
$0.334\;e\,\mathrm{\AA}^{-3}$. We compare the Fraser 1978 displaced volumes
with the Pontius 1996 protein-core group means. The full FoXS reciprocal
excluded-solvent convention has a different q dependence and is not selected here.
Implicit hydrogens contribute both electrons and their group volume without
adding overlapping hydrogen centres. The deposited coordinates are never
rescaled.

Hydration uses the validated Pepsi 3 spatial-shell grid and bonded-water
form factor. The fixed control uses contrast
$0.0135\;e\,\mathrm{\AA}^{-3}$. Shell points have effective weights
$h^3\rho_s$ with the default 3 Å grid spacing; fractional atomic exposure
does not set their weights. pySEB performs these calculations internally;
FoXS and Pepsi-SAXS remain optional external validation tools, not runtime
dependencies.

The [saved calculation](data/titin-results/results.json) records the
results with this convention. Fixed hydration improves the Fraser training
reduced chi-squared from 55.213 to 43.953. Solvent refinement reaches 23.711,
but hits the hydration bound and the evaluation limit. This remains a poor
structural fit despite the independently validated hydration calculation.

### Separate the three scattering contributions

For each heavy-atom group, the amplitude has the schematic form

$$b_i(q)=f_i(q)-\rho_s V_i(q)+\Delta\rho_h H_i(q).$$

The first term scatters in vacuum, the second subtracts displaced bulk water,
and the third adds the hydration contrast around exposed groups. We will
switch these terms on in controls before fitting solvent parameters. The
hydration-only control is diagnostic; the complete solution model includes
both displaced solvent and hydration.

We use the validated Pepsi 3 spatial hydration convention: a grid of shell
points around each domain, with bonded-water form factors. Its effective point
weights include the reference bulk-density prefactor; they are not physical
water voxel volumes. This matches the hydration component independently of
fitting this experimental curve. The atomic and displaced-solvent conventions
still have small differences from Pepsi.

### Precompute the expensive cloud terms

Each domain contains 688 heavy-atom groups plus spatial hydration points.
Cloud construction calculates exposure, shell geometry, and pair distances once. Fixed
controls are then evaluated on a dense q grid and interpolated during the
linker fit. The later solvent refinement changes only amplitudes, reusing the
same exposure and geometry caches.

```{python}
#| tags: [titin-generation]
#| eval: false
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Build the atomic clouds and evaluate the six controls"
ensemble_path = data_directory / "1TIU-heavy-ensemble.pdb"
ensemble_models = (1, 7, 13, 19)
cache_q = np.linspace(0.0, q.max(), 401)

atomic_profiles = {
    "fraser": pyseb.AtomicSAXSParameterProfile.protein_defaults(
        pyseb.AtomicSAXSVolumeModel.Fraser1978
    ),
    "pontius": pyseb.AtomicSAXSParameterProfile.protein_defaults(
        pyseb.AtomicSAXSVolumeModel.Pontius1996
    ),
}


def empty_atomic_cache():
    return {
        "form_factor": [],
        "n_amplitude": [],
        "c_amplitude": [],
        "nc_phase": [],
        "rg2": [],
        "n_sigma2": [],
        "c_sigma2": [],
        "nc_sigma2": [],
    }


parsed_ensemble = {}
for model_number in ensemble_models:
    parse_options = pyseb.StructureParseOptions()
    parse_options.model_number = model_number
    parsed_ensemble[model_number] = pyseb.PDBParser().parse_file(
        str(ensemble_path), parse_options
    )


atomic_sources = {name: [] for name in atomic_profiles}
for profile_name, profile in atomic_profiles.items():
    for model_number, atoms in parsed_ensemble.items():
        alpha_carbons = [atom for atom in atoms if atom.atom_name == "CA"]

        build_options = pyseb.AtomicSAXSCloudBuildOptions()
        build_options.calculate_solvent_accessibility = True
        build_options.sasa_probe_radius = 1.4
        build_options.sasa_point_count = 960
        build_options.reference_atom_serials = {
            "nterminus": alpha_carbons[0].serial,
            "cterminus": alpha_carbons[-1].serial,
        }

        initial_options = pyseb.AtomicSAXSOptions()
        initial_options.solvent_electron_density = 0.334
        initial_options.hydration_model = pyseb.AtomicSAXSHydrationModel.SpatialShell
        initial_options.hydration_water_model = pyseb.AtomicSAXSHydrationWaterModel.BondedWater
        build_options.hydration_shell_convention = pyseb.AtomicSAXSHydrationShellConvention.Pepsi3
        cloud = pyseb.AtomicSAXSCloudBuilder.build(
            atoms, profile, initial_options, build_options
        )
        cloud_world = pyseb.World(
            f"I27{profile_name.title()}Model{model_number}"
        )
        cloud_world.Add(cloud, "domain")
        atomic_sources[profile_name].append((cloud, cloud_world))


def evaluate_atomic_ensemble(
    profile_name,
    q_values,
    include_excluded_solvent,
    excluded_volume_scale,
    include_hydration,
    hydration_shell_contrast,
):
    cache = empty_atomic_cache()
    q_values = np.asarray(q_values, dtype=float)
    q_list = q_values.tolist()

    for cloud, cloud_world in atomic_sources[profile_name]:
        options = cloud.get_options()
        options.solvent_electron_density = 0.334
        options.include_excluded_solvent = include_excluded_solvent
        options.excluded_volume_scale = excluded_volume_scale
        options.include_hydration = include_hydration
        options.hydration_shell_contrast = hydration_shell_contrast
        options.hydration_volume_per_exposed_atom = 30.0
        cloud.set_options(options)

        cache["form_factor"].append(
            cloud_world.EvaluateFormFactor("domain", {}, q_list)
        )
        cache["n_amplitude"].append(
            cloud_world.EvaluateFormFactorAmplitude(
                "domain.nterminus", {}, q_list
            )
        )
        cache["c_amplitude"].append(
            cloud_world.EvaluateFormFactorAmplitude(
                "domain.cterminus", {}, q_list
            )
        )
        cache["nc_phase"].append(
            cloud_world.EvaluatePhaseFactor(
                "domain.nterminus", "domain.cterminus", {}, q_list
            )
        )
        cache["rg2"].append(
            cloud_world.EvaluateRadiusOfGyration2("domain", {})
        )
        cache["n_sigma2"].append(
            cloud_world.EvaluateSMSDRef2Scat("domain.nterminus", {})
        )
        cache["c_sigma2"].append(
            cloud_world.EvaluateSMSDRef2Scat("domain.cterminus", {})
        )
        cache["nc_sigma2"].append(
            cloud_world.EvaluateSMSDRef2Ref(
                "domain.nterminus", "domain.cterminus", {}
            )
        )
    return cache


solvent_controls = {
    "vacuum": {
        "label": "vacuum",
        "profile": "fraser",
        "excluded": False,
        "hydration": False,
    },
    "fraser_excluded": {
        "label": "Fraser excluded solvent",
        "profile": "fraser",
        "excluded": True,
        "hydration": False,
    },
    "pontius_excluded": {
        "label": "Pontius excluded solvent",
        "profile": "pontius",
        "excluded": True,
        "hydration": False,
    },
    "hydration_only": {
        "label": "hydration only",
        "profile": "fraser",
        "excluded": False,
        "hydration": True,
    },
    "fraser_complete": {
        "label": "Fraser plus hydration",
        "profile": "fraser",
        "excluded": True,
        "hydration": True,
    },
    "pontius_complete": {
        "label": "Pontius plus hydration",
        "profile": "pontius",
        "excluded": True,
        "hydration": True,
    },
}

atomic_caches = {}
for control_name, control in solvent_controls.items():
    atomic_caches[control_name] = evaluate_atomic_ensemble(
        control["profile"],
        cache_q,
        control["excluded"],
        1.0,
        control["hydration"],
        0.0135,
    )

print(f"NMR conformations retained: {len(ensemble_models)}")
print(
    "Atomic plus shell scatterers per cloud: "
    f"{atomic_sources['fraser'][0][0].scatterer_count()}"
)
```

```{python}
print(f"NMR conformations retained: {len(results['ensemble_models'])}")
print(f"Atomic plus shell points per cloud: {results['atomic_scatterer_count']}")
```

Each averaged form factor describes one domain selected from the four-model
ensemble. The two terminal amplitudes and their phase factor retain distinct
N- and C-terminal reference points. Averaging these quantities separately
means the two I27 copies are independently selected from that ensemble when
pySEB constructs their interference terms.

```{python}
#| tags: [titin-generation]
#| eval: false
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Connect ensemble-averaged domain callbacks"
def interpolate_atomic_cache(cache, q_grid=cache_q):
    return {
        "form_factor": CubicSpline(
            q_grid, np.mean(cache["form_factor"], axis=0)
        ),
        "n_amplitude": CubicSpline(
            q_grid, np.mean(cache["n_amplitude"], axis=0)
        ),
        "c_amplitude": CubicSpline(
            q_grid, np.mean(cache["c_amplitude"], axis=0)
        ),
        "nc_phase": CubicSpline(
            q_grid, np.mean(cache["nc_phase"], axis=0)
        ),
        "rg2": np.mean(cache["rg2"]),
        "n_sigma2": np.mean(cache["n_sigma2"]),
        "c_sigma2": np.mean(cache["c_sigma2"]),
        "nc_sigma2": np.mean(cache["nc_sigma2"]),
    }


atomic_ensembles = {
    mode: interpolate_atomic_cache(cache)
    for mode, cache in atomic_caches.items()
}


def ensemble_domain(ensemble):
    domain = pyseb.NumericalSubunit(pyseb.NormalizationMode.Normalized)
    domain.addReferencePoint("nterminus")
    domain.addReferencePoint("cterminus")
    domain.setTotalBeta(domain_beta)
    domain.setFormFactorFunction(
        lambda q_value, parameters: float(
            ensemble["form_factor"](q_value)
        )
    )
    domain.setFormFactorAmplitudeFunction(
        "nterminus",
        lambda q_value, parameters: float(
            ensemble["n_amplitude"](q_value)
        ),
    )
    domain.setFormFactorAmplitudeFunction(
        "cterminus",
        lambda q_value, parameters: float(
            ensemble["c_amplitude"](q_value)
        ),
    )
    domain.setPhaseFactorFunction(
        "nterminus",
        "cterminus",
        lambda q_value, parameters: float(
            ensemble["nc_phase"](q_value)
        ),
    )
    domain.setRadiusOfGyration2Provider(
        lambda parameters: ensemble["rg2"]
    )
    domain.setSigmaMSDRef2ScatProvider(
        "nterminus",
        lambda parameters: ensemble["n_sigma2"],
    )
    domain.setSigmaMSDRef2ScatProvider(
        "cterminus",
        lambda parameters: ensemble["c_sigma2"],
    )
    domain.setSigmaMSDRef2RefProvider(
        "nterminus",
        "cterminus",
        lambda parameters: ensemble["nc_sigma2"],
    )
    domain.ValidateNumerically({})
    return domain


def atomic_titin_world(ensemble, name):
    domain1 = ensemble_domain(ensemble)
    domain2 = ensemble_domain(ensemble)
    world = pyseb.World(name)
    graph = world.Add(domain1, "domain1")
    world.Link(
        "GaussianPolymer", "ntail.end2", "domain1.nterminus"
    )
    world.Link(
        "GaussianPolymer", "linker.end1", "domain1.cterminus"
    )
    world.Link(
        domain2, "domain2.nterminus", "linker.end2"
    )
    world.Link(
        "GaussianPolymer", "ctail.end1", "domain2.cterminus"
    )
    world.Add(graph, "titin")
    return world


atomic_worlds = {
    name: atomic_titin_world(
        ensemble, f"TitinAtomic{name.title()}"
    )
    for (name, ensemble) in atomic_ensembles.items()
}
```

### Fit the cached ensemble

The four fitted variables match round 2: linker $R_g$, terminal-chain
$R_{g,8}$, intensity scale, and background. The PDB coordinates remain fixed.
The optimizer sees an ordinary linked pySEB structure; only the numerical
domain callbacks now read from ensemble-averaged curves.

```{python}
#| tags: [titin-generation]
#| eval: false
def atomic_curve(world, values, q_values):
    linker_rg, tail_rg8, scale, background = values
    parameters = construct_polymer_parameters(linker_rg, tail_rg8)
    form_factor = np.asarray(
        world.EvaluateFormFactor(
            "titin", parameters, q_values.tolist()
        )
    )
    return scale * form_factor + background


def fit_atomic_world(world):
    return least_squares(
        lambda values: (
            atomic_curve(world, values, fit_q) - fit_intensity
        ) / fit_uncertainty,
        x0=[5.0, 5.0, 0.033, 0.0002],
        bounds=(
            [linker_rg_bounds[0], 0.1, 0.0, 0.0],
            [linker_rg_bounds[1], 30.0, 1.0, 0.01],
        ),
        x_scale="jac",
    )


atomic_names = [
    "linker Rg [A]",
    "terminal-chain Rg8 [A]",
    "scale",
    "background",
]
fixed_atomic_fits = {
    name: fit_atomic_world(world)
    for name, world in atomic_worlds.items()
}


def atomic_split_chi2(world, values, number_of_parameters):
    training_residual = (
        atomic_curve(world, values, fit_q) - fit_intensity
    ) / fit_uncertainty
    held_residual = (
        atomic_curve(world, values, held_q) - held_intensity
    ) / held_uncertainty
    return (
        reduced_chi_squared(training_residual, number_of_parameters),
        reduced_chi_squared(held_residual, 0),
    )


fixed_metrics = {}
fixed_rows = [
    "| Fixed atomic control | training reduced chi^2 | held-out mean squared residual |",
    "| --- | ---: | ---: |",
]
for name, control in solvent_controls.items():
    fit = fixed_atomic_fits[name]
    training_chi2, held_chi2 = atomic_split_chi2(
        atomic_worlds[name], fit.x, fit.x.size
    )
    fixed_metrics[name] = (training_chi2, held_chi2)
    fixed_rows.append(
        f"| {control['label']} | {training_chi2:.3f} | {held_chi2:.3f} |"
    )

display(Markdown("\n".join(fixed_rows)))
```

These are fixed-physics controls: the excluded-volume multiplier is exactly
1.0 and the enabled hydration contrast is exactly
$+0.0135\;e\,\mathrm{\AA}^{-3}$. Only the linker, terminal-chain, intensity
scale, and background were fitted. The alternating q points were not seen by
the optimizer.

### Look at an atomic realization before interpreting hydration

The fitted domains above are averages of scattering functions, which have no
single set of coordinates. For visualization we rebuild the same topology with
two copies of NMR model 1 and use the fitted chain sizes. This scene illustrates
one representative geometry, not the full four-model average. Hydration changes
the explicit shell-point amplitudes, which are included in the hydrated scene
as smaller purple markers. The dry scene contains atomic groups only.

```{python}
#| tags: [titin-generation]
#| eval: false
def atomic_visual_world(profile_name, hydrated):
    atoms = parsed_ensemble[1]
    ca = [atom for atom in atoms if atom.atom_name == "CA"]
    build = pyseb.AtomicSAXSCloudBuildOptions()
    build.calculate_solvent_accessibility = True
    build.sasa_probe_radius = 1.4
    build.sasa_point_count = 960
    build.reference_atom_serials = {
        "nterminus": ca[0].serial, "cterminus": ca[-1].serial}
    options = pyseb.AtomicSAXSOptions()
    options.solvent_electron_density = 0.334
    # A dry scene contains atomic groups only; the hydrated scene adds shell points.
    options.hydration_model = (
        pyseb.AtomicSAXSHydrationModel.SpatialShell if hydrated
        else pyseb.AtomicSAXSHydrationModel.AtomCentered
    )
    options.hydration_water_model = pyseb.AtomicSAXSHydrationWaterModel.BondedWater
    build.hydration_shell_convention = pyseb.AtomicSAXSHydrationShellConvention.Pepsi3
    options.include_excluded_solvent = True
    options.include_hydration = hydrated
    options.hydration_shell_contrast = 0.0135
    options.hydration_volume_per_exposed_atom = 30.0
    domains = [pyseb.AtomicSAXSCloudBuilder.build(
        atoms, atomic_profiles[profile_name], options, build) for _ in range(2)]
    world = pyseb.World("AtomicVisualization")
    graph = world.Add(domains[0], "domain1")
    world.Link("GaussianPolymer", "ntail.end2", "domain1.nterminus")
    world.Link("GaussianPolymer", "linker.end1", "domain1.cterminus")
    world.Link(domains[1], "domain2.nterminus", "linker.end2")
    world.Link("GaussianPolymer", "ctail.end1", "domain2.cterminus")
    world.Add(graph, "titin")
    return world

for hydrated, control in [(False, "fraser_excluded"), (True, "fraser_complete")]:
    show_structure(atomic_visual_world("fraser", hydrated),
                   construct_polymer_parameters(*fixed_atomic_fits[control].x[:2]),
                   "atomic-hydrated" if hydrated else "atomic-displaced-solvent")

compare_curves({
    solvent_controls[name]["label"]: atomic_curve(
        atomic_worlds[name], fixed_atomic_fits[name].x, q)
    for name in ("vacuum", "fraser_excluded", "fraser_complete")
})

for profile in ("fraser", "pontius"):
    dry = fixed_metrics[f"{profile}_excluded"][1]
```

### Refine the complete solvent models within physical bounds

We now fit the Fraser-plus-hydration and Pontius-plus-hydration models again,
adding only two tightly bounded solvent variables. The excluded-volume
multiplier is restricted to $0.95^3$--$1.05^3$ and hydration contrast to
$-0.027$--$+0.054\;e\,\mathrm{\AA}^{-3}$. Exact Debye profiles are evaluated
at every solvent trial; a small memoization cache avoids repeating them when
the optimizer perturbs only linker or intensity parameters.

```{python}
#| tags: [titin-generation]
#| eval: false
excluded_bounds = (0.95**3, 1.05**3)
hydration_bounds = (-0.027, 0.054)
solvent_world_cache = {"fraser": {}, "pontius": {}}


def solvent_world(profile_name, excluded_scale, hydration_contrast, q_grid):
    q_grid = np.asarray(q_grid, dtype=float)
    cache_key = (
        float(excluded_scale),
        float(hydration_contrast),
        q_grid.size,
        float(q_grid[0]),
        float(q_grid[-1]),
    )
    cached = solvent_world_cache[profile_name].get(cache_key)
    if cached is not None:
        return cached

    evaluation_q = np.unique(np.concatenate(([0.0], q_grid)))
    cache = evaluate_atomic_ensemble(
        profile_name,
        evaluation_q,
        True,
        excluded_scale,
        True,
        hydration_contrast,
    )
    ensemble = interpolate_atomic_cache(cache, evaluation_q)
    world = atomic_titin_world(
        ensemble,
        f"TitinAtomicRefined{profile_name.title()}",
    )
    solvent_world_cache[profile_name][cache_key] = world
    return world


def refined_atomic_curve(profile_name, values, q_values):
    excluded_scale, hydration_contrast = values[4:6]
    world = solvent_world(
        profile_name, excluded_scale, hydration_contrast, q_values
    )
    return atomic_curve(world, values[:4], q_values)


def fit_complete_solvent_model(profile_name):
    fixed = fixed_atomic_fits[f"{profile_name}_complete"]
    return least_squares(
        lambda values: (
            refined_atomic_curve(profile_name, values, fit_q)
            - fit_intensity
        ) / fit_uncertainty,
        x0=np.concatenate((fixed.x, [1.0, 0.0135])),
        bounds=(
            [linker_rg_bounds[0], 0.1, 0.0, 0.0,
             excluded_bounds[0], hydration_bounds[0]],
            [linker_rg_bounds[1], 30.0, 1.0, 0.01,
             excluded_bounds[1], hydration_bounds[1]],
        ),
        x_scale=[5.0, 5.0, 0.03, 0.001, 0.1, 0.02],
        max_nfev=30,
    )


refined_fits = {
    profile_name: fit_complete_solvent_model(profile_name)
    for profile_name in ("fraser", "pontius")
}


def solvent_parameter_at_bound(values):
    tolerances = (1.0e-4, 1.0e-4)
    pairs = (
        (values[4], excluded_bounds),
        (values[5], hydration_bounds),
    )
    return any(
        abs(value - lower) <= tolerance
        or abs(value - upper) <= tolerance
        for ((value, (lower, upper)), tolerance) in zip(pairs, tolerances)
    )


refined_models = {}
refined_metrics = {}
refined_rows = [
    "| Complete model | volume multiplier | hydration contrast | "
    "training reduced chi^2 | held-out mean squared residual | accepted improvement? |",
    "| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | :---: |",
]
for profile_name, fit in refined_fits.items():
    final_world = solvent_world(profile_name, fit.x[4], fit.x[5], q)
    final_curve = atomic_curve(final_world, fit.x[:4], q)
    refined_models[profile_name] = final_curve

    training_residual = (
        final_curve[::2] - fit_intensity
    ) / fit_uncertainty
    held_residual = (
        final_curve[1::2] - held_intensity
    ) / held_uncertainty
    training_chi2 = reduced_chi_squared(training_residual, fit.x.size)
    held_chi2 = reduced_chi_squared(held_residual, 0)
    reached_bound = solvent_parameter_at_bound(fit.x)
    fixed_held = fixed_metrics[f"{profile_name}_complete"][1]
    accepted = fit.success and held_chi2 < fixed_held and not reached_bound
    print(f"{profile_name.title()} optimizer: {fit.message}")
    refined_metrics[profile_name] = {
        "training": training_chi2,
        "held": held_chi2,
        "reached_bound": reached_bound,
        "accepted": accepted,
    }
    refined_rows.append(
        f"| {profile_name.title()} plus hydration | {fit.x[4]:.6f} | "
        f"{fit.x[5]:+.6f} | {training_chi2:.3f} | {held_chi2:.3f} | "
        f"{'yes' if accepted else 'no'} |"
    )

display(Markdown("\n".join(refined_rows)))
```

```{python}
rows = ["| Complete model | Volume multiplier | Hydration contrast | Training reduced chi² | Held-point score | Accepted improvement? |",
        "| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | :---: |"]
for profile in ("fraser", "pontius"):
    fit = results["fits"][f"refined_{profile}"]
    metrics = results["refined_metrics"][profile]
    print(f"{profile.title()} optimizer: {fit['message']}")
    rows.append(f"| {profile.title()} plus hydration | {fit['x'][4]:.6f} | "
                f"{fit['x'][5]:+.6f} | {fit['training_reduced_chi2']:.3f} | "
                f"{fit['held_score']:.3f} | {'yes' if metrics['accepted'] else 'no'} |")
display(Markdown("\n".join(rows)))
```

“Accepted improvement” is intentionally stricter than a lower training loss:
the held-out mean squared standardized residual must also improve relative to the matching fixed
complete model, the optimizer must converge, and neither solvent parameter
may finish at a bound. This is a practical screening rule, not a formal
statistical significance test. The table
uses a $10^{-4}$ bound tolerance and reports the result instead of assuming in
advance that either published volume convention must fit this dataset better.

## Compare the rounds

```{python}
#| label: fig-linked-titin-fits
#| fig-cap: "Analytical and hybrid cloud fits with standardized experimental residuals; curves loaded from saved calculations."
spheroid_model = curves["analytical_constrained"]
ca_model = curves["debye"]
vacuum_model = curves["fixed_vacuum"]
fraser_model = curves["refined_fraser"]
pontius_model = curves["refined_pontius"]
figure, (axis, residual_axis) = plt.subplots(
    2,
    1,
    figsize=(7.2, 7.0),
    sharex=True,
    gridspec_kw={"height_ratios": [3, 1]},
)

axis.errorbar(
    q,
    intensity,
    yerr=uncertainty,
    fmt=".",
    markersize=3,
    color="black",
    alpha=0.65,
    label="SASDKC2 experiment",
)
axis.plot(q, spheroid_model, label="Spheroid--polymer--spheroid")
axis.plot(q, ca_model, label="688-point heavy-atom Debye clouds")
axis.plot(q, vacuum_model, label="Atomic ensemble: vacuum form factors")
axis.plot(q, fraser_model, label="Atomic ensemble: refined Fraser solvent")
axis.plot(q, pontius_model, label="Atomic ensemble: refined Pontius solvent")
axis.set_yscale("log")
axis.set_ylabel("Intensity [a.u.]")
axis.legend()

residual_axis.axhline(0.0, color="0.5", linewidth=1)
residual_axis.plot(
    q,
    (spheroid_model - intensity) / uncertainty,
    label="spheroid residual",
)
residual_axis.plot(
    q,
    (ca_model - intensity) / uncertainty,
    label="Debye-cloud residual",
)
residual_axis.plot(
    q,
    (vacuum_model - intensity) / uncertainty,
    label="atomic-vacuum residual",
)
residual_axis.plot(
    q,
    (fraser_model - intensity) / uncertainty,
    label="atomic-Fraser residual",
)
residual_axis.plot(
    q,
    (pontius_model - intensity) / uncertainty,
    label="atomic-Pontius residual",
)
residual_axis.set_xlabel(r"$q\;[\mathrm{\AA}^{-1}]$")
residual_axis.set_ylabel(r"$(I_{model}-I)/\sigma$")
residual_axis.legend(fontsize="small")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

The six fixed controls separate vacuum form factors, displaced solvent, and
hydration instead of attributing every change to one combined correction. The
two refined models then ask whether a tightly bounded adjustment is supported
outside the training points. Read the rendered tables for the numerical
answer: no conclusion about Fraser versus Pontius is inserted before those
training and held-out values are calculated.

More coordinates do **not** automatically make a better solution model. The
atomic rounds still omit atomistic conformations for the construct tails and
linker, and correlations between linker extension and domain orientation.
Their fitted linker and terminal-chain sizes, backgrounds, and structured
residuals show how the remaining model compensates for those omissions even
when the deposited coordinates are held fixed.

This is the main lesson of the three rounds. A PDB cloud is a more detailed
representation, but only a better scattering model when its solution-state
assumptions are also better. The [deposited SASBDB fit](https://www.sasbdb.org/data/SASDKC2/)
reports $\chi^2=1.068$; that result is a useful benchmark, not a value these
pedagogical pySEB models are expected to reproduce.
